name: IP geolocation
plain: The server converts the visitor's IP into an approximate country, region and city.
meaning: Commercial databases (MaxMind, IPinfo, IP2Location) map IPs to places. Vendors claim about 99.8% country accuracy, but city accuracy is much lower and mobile or VPN IPs often point to the carrier hub or exit.

web.api: GeoIP lookup of the client IP (MaxMind GeoIP2, IPinfo)

steps: Query a local or API database
Return country, region, city, postal, lat and long

data.metric: Country, region, city, lat and long with accuracy radius

fields.name: accuracy radius
fields.precision: city level in good cases, vendor reported

limits.headline: Can guess your country, region and city from your IP address
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when your device connects to the site
can: Look up a likely country, region and city from your IP
Show local content, prices and language
Spot a mismatch with your time zone, such as when you use a VPN
cannot: Find your street or home; city guesses are much less exact than country
Get it right on mobile and VPN connections, which often point to a carrier hub or exit
Know your name or account from it
limits.reach_label: Country is close, city is rough

story.what_it_is: A site turns your internet address into a guess of your country, region and city.
story.for_you: You never have to allow anything. Sites guess your country and often your city from your internet address. It is right for countries most of the time, less for cities. A VPN changes the guess.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for local prices, language, taxes and rights. Ads use it for regional targeting. Fraud teams compare it with your billing address and sign in history.

use_cases.example: A game site picks your server region and shows local store prices.
A cloud gaming service uses it to see which data center is close to you and whether the game is licensed in your country.
A streaming service uses it to show only the shows allowed in your country.
A store shows prices, taxes and delivery for your country.
An ad network shows local ads for your city, such as nearby store offers.
A bank flags a login from a country the customer has never visited.
A site measures where its readers live without asking them.

technical_bounds: City accuracy varies widely and is often wrong for mobile and VPN users

value.legit_uses: Content localization, tax and licensing, fraud rules
value.abuse: Price discrimination, geoblocking, stalking via leaked city
